name: North Macedonia
summary_text: North Macedonia is workable for trans visitors. Nothing is criminalised, and Skopje hosts both Pride and an organised Trans March for Visibility (TransFormA, March 2024) — public trans organising that proceeds without serious incident. Anti-discrimination law covers sexual orientation and gender identity (2019 amendments). Counterweights: hate speech and hate crimes remain common with no effective justice-system response (European Commission), social-media death threats are routine, and there is no legal gender recognition. For a visitor: no legal exposure; small but functioning community; standard Balkan street-hostility caution.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2024 (covering 2023) chapter on North Macedonia: hate speech remained serious with no meaningful state response despite countless reports (echoed by the European Commission's country report); in September the Basic Criminal Court of Skopje sentenced a man to two years for assaulting an LGBTI activist, applying SOGI aggravating grounds; ECRI called for a ban on nonconsensual intersex surgeries; anti-gender movement gained ground, including campaigns against a school handout showing a gay couple.

sources.title: ‘We march bravely’: Transgender Day of Visibility marked in North Macedonia · Global Voices
sources.claim_summary: Global Voices (March 2024): 'We march bravely' - Transgender Day of Visibility marked in North Macedonia with a March for Visibility of Trans People in Skopje organised by TransFormA; notes a worrisome trend of mobilising religious institutions to scapegoat this small vulnerable group.

ILGA-Europe/ERA LGBTI Enlargement Review 2024: country submissions from Western Balkans and Eastern Partnership countries (including North Macedonia) with top priorities, feedback on the European Commission's 2023 Enlargement Report, and recommendations to the EU.
US State Department 2019 Human Rights Report for North Macedonia: official assessment including the SOGI section - anti-discrimination law, societal violence and discrimination against LGBT persons.

sources.title: Anti-LGBTQ discrimination harms economies of Serbia, North Macedonia
sources.claim_summary: Washington Blade (Oct 2023): 'Anti-LGBTQ discrimination harms economies of Serbia, North Macedonia' - economic analysis of the cost of discrimination in the Balkans.

sources.title: Macedonia Gay Rights Record 'Worst in Balkans' | Balkan Insight
sources.claim_summary: Balkan Insight (Feb 2012): ILGA-Europe's Rainbow Europe Index put Macedonia at the bottom of the Balkans with a score of -2 (scale 17 to -7) - the only Balkan country in the 'red zone' of worst offenders, characterised by 'gross violations of human rights and discrimination'.

sources.title: Macedonia Moves to Rule Out Same-Sex Marriage | Balkan Insight
sources.claim_summary: Balkan Insight (July 2014): Macedonia's government submitted a constitutional motion to define marriage strictly as a union of one man and one woman, ruling out same-sex marriage and gay adoption - needing two-thirds of MPs, with the conservative DPA expected to provide the extra votes.
